messages:
maria: heads-up, bringing a new community model 'Pelago-6B' for eval. quick legal question before we start quant experiments - license attached below.

maria: license excerpt: `NonCommercial Redistribution Prohibited; Attribution Required; No Warranty`

maria: tl;dr: can we run quantization and store quantized weights on dedicated infra for customers on paid plans? also curious about shipping a quantized wheel/container to on-prem customers.

sam: @maria thanks — short answer: 'NonCommercial' is a flag. If license literally prohibits commercial use, we can't offer it to paying customers. need to see full license text though.

maria: pasted full header in thread DM. this is the repo header: `Pelago Public License v0.9 (PPL-0.9) — grants research/educational use, prohibits commercial exploitation.`

ezra: second question from infra: even if allowed, does redistribution include sending quantized weights in a docker image? some licences treat transformed weights differently.

sam: correct. many licenses differentiate "derivative weights" vs "model output". If PPL forbids commercial use or redistribution, shipping quantized checkpoints to customers likely violates redistrib rule.

license-bot: automated-check: detected phrase 'NonCommercial' and 'No Redistribution' in header. Recommendation: consult legal for commercial use.

maria: we need explicit guidance because product wants to run evals on dedicated and potentially offer a managed endpoint for early access customers. can we at least run internal benchmarking and quantize for research?

sam: internal benchmarking + evals -> usually OK under research exceptions, but depends on wording. If it allows internal evaluation, fine. Public-facing or paid features are blocked.

todd: technically we can keep quantized artifacts inside our private clusters (no customer access) and use them to power hosted endpoints for internal testing. but if customers hit them or we distribute, that's risky.

maria: what's the path forward? options I see: 1) ask upstream for a commercial license 2) pick a different model 3) negotiate narrow OEM terms 4) run hosted-only evals and don't expose weights.

sam: yes. also check export control language — some models have extra clauses requiring attribution notices in UI, or restrictions on derivatives. If attribution required, we must display credit in our docs/console.

ezra: for experimental benching, can we run quantized perf tests that log metrics but never persist the checkpoint to disk? ephemeral in-memory only?

sam: ephemeral runtime transformations for internal evals are low risk. But if any checkpoint or cached KV is written to logs/backups and could be exported, that's a problem. Make sure retention is zero and access limited.

maria: noted. I'll pause any customer-facing work. @sam can you draft a quick email template to request a commercial license/clarification from Pelago maintainers? I'll attach our intended use (dedicated hosted endpoints, quantization for latency/cost).

sam: yep. I'll send a templated ask: include: intended usage, quantization levels, redistribution plans (none unless licensed), commercial sale details, attribution text placement.

license-bot: suggested snippet: `We are Redwood Inference. We intend to use Pelago-6B for hosted inference for paying customers. Please confirm whether PPL-0.9 permits commercial hosting, derivative quantized weights, and redistribution to on-prem customers. If not permitted, please provide commercial licensing options.`

maria: perfect. thanks. one more: anyone seen prior precedence for buying a commercial add-on from a community model that then allowed shipping quantized weights?

todd: yes — we did that for 'Cedar' last year. vendor provided a commercial license addendum allowing redistribution of quantized weights under an SLA. ops handled key rotation and watermarking.

sam: we'll go that route if Pelago maintainers are open. otherwise pick a permissively licensed alternative.

maria: ok pausing onboarding until legal gets a reply. tagging @ezra to keep test harnesses on hold. :hand::skin-tone-3:

ezra: ack, will pause. will prepare a list of exact quant configs we want to test (4-bit/8-bit/FP16) to include in the license ask.

maria: thanks all, closing out for now. will post updates when we hear back.
